stories.headline: AWS and NVIDIA to Deliver 2 Million Additional GPUs and Next-Generation Infrastructure for Agentic and Physical AI
stories.new_information: AWS and NVIDIA to Deliver 2 Million Additional GPUs and Next-Generation Infrastructure for Agentic and Physical AI. Building on already-rapid customer adoption of NVIDIA-accelerated compute on AWS, the companies plan to deploy 2 million additional NVIDIA GPUs across AWS’s global infrastructure and deepen their work together across AI factories, CPUs, networking, open models, data processing and robotics, delivering co-engineered AI solutions that enable customers to accelerate AI development and deployment at unprecedented scale.
stories.impact_chain: Direct: AI Models/Applications, Compute, HBM/Memory, Networking/Optical, Data Centers. Second-order: Power/Electrical, Cooling.

evidence_sources.title: AWS and NVIDIA to Deliver 2 Million Additional GPUs and Next-Generation Infrastructure for Agentic and Physical AI

facts: AWS and NVIDIA to Deliver 2 Million Additional GPUs and Next-Generation Infrastructure for Agentic and Physical AI

Building on already-rapid customer adoption of NVIDIA-accelerated compute on AWS, the companies plan to deploy 2 million additional NVIDIA GPUs across AWS’s global infrastructure and deepen their work together across AI factories, CPUs, networking, open models, data processing and robotics, delivering co-engineered AI solutions that enable customers to accelerate AI development and deployment at unprecedented scale.

As part of the expanded collaboration, the companies are working to: Deploy 2 million additional NVIDIA GPUs across AWS’s global infrastructure in 2027-2028 Bring NVIDIA Vera CPU‑based infrastructure to AWS Extend NVIDIA NVLink Fusion™ with custom NVIDIA high‑bandwidth memory (NVHBM) Build AI factories for the U.S.

facts: For providers serving latency-sensitive, high-volume inference workloads, NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX provides a path to deploy differentiated compute in proven rack-scale systems.
An extension of the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, Groq 3 LPX delivers a major boost in AI inference by enabling ultrafast token generation for highly responsive agentic systems.

It delivered a record 3,400 output tokens per second in Artificial Analysis benchmarking running Gemma 4 31B, an open source agentic model, with a 100,000-token context critical for agentic systems — the fastest performance ever recorded for the model.

Multimodal clinical data can improve diagnostics, discovery, and operational efficiency.

biotech.risks: FDA filing acceptance is not approval; manufacturing, safety, durability and commercialization risks remain.
